# Conditional Statements


## If statements

```{python}
import numpy as np
from jupyprint import jupyprint

coin_flip = np.random.choice(['HEADS', 'TAILS'])

coin_flip
```

```{python}
if coin_flip == 'TAILS':
    print('You got tails!')
```

```{python}
if coin_flip == 'HEADS':
    print('You got heads!')
```

Why do we only see one print out?

```{python}
if True:
    print('The condition is True!')
```

```{python}
if False:
    print('We NEVER see this printout!')
```

```{python}
coin_flip = np.random.choice(['HEADS', 'TAILS'])

if coin_flip == 'TAILS':
    print('You got tails!')

if coin_flip == 'HEADS':
    print('You got heads!')
```

## Else statements


```{python}
coin_flip = np.random.choice(['HEADS', 'TAILS'])

if coin_flip == 'TAILS':
    print('You got TAILS!')

else:
    print('You got HEADS!')
```

## Elif statements

```{python}
three_way_coin_flip = np.random.choice(["HEADS", "TAILS", "BODY"])

three_way_coin_flip 
```

```{python}
three_way_coin_flip = np.random.choice(["HEADS", "TAILS", "BODY"])

if three_way_coin_flip == 'TAILS':
    print('You got TAILS!')

elif three_way_coin_flip == 'HEADS':
    print('You got HEADS!')
    
else:
    print('You got BODY!')
```

## Dice Guessing - a simple multi-player game...

[Demonstrates if, else etc with comparison operators]

[Two people send guesses about a dice roll from their laptops]

[I roll a dice with `np.random.randint(1, 7)` then use conditionals to say who won (who is *closer* to roll), and to keep score]


[Do game first manually]

[Point out random.randint documentation: "Return random integers from `low` (inclusive) to `high` (exclusive)."]

```{python}
# One dice roll.
np.random.randint(low = 1,
                  high= 7)
```

```{python}
# Make it look nicer.
import numpy as np
from IPython.display import display, HTML

roll = np.random.randint(1, 7)

roll_to_index_list = roll - 1

dice = ["⚀", "⚁", "⚂", "⚃", "⚄", "⚅"][roll_to_index_list]

jupyprint(f'<h1>{dice}</h1><p>The roll was <b style="color:red;">{roll}</b></p>')
```

```{python}
student_1_name = "Dave"

student_2_name = "Krystal"
```

```{python}
student_1_money = 100

student_2_money = 100
```

```{python}
student_1_bet = 3

student_2_bet = 5
```

```{python}
# Random dice roll, then win/lose money
roll = np.random.randint(1, 7)

roll_to_index_list = roll - 1

dice = ["⚀", "⚁", "⚂", "⚃", "⚄", "⚅"][roll_to_index_list]

jupyprint(f'<h1>{dice}</h1><p>The roll was <b style="color:red;">{roll}</b></p>')

student_1_diff = abs(student_1_bet - roll)

student_2_diff = abs(student_2_bet - roll)

jupyprint(f'<b>{student_1_name} bet {student_1_bet}.</b>')
jupyprint(f'<b>{student_2_name} bet {student_2_bet}.</b>')

if student_1_diff == student_2_diff:
    jupyprint(f'<h1>Draw!</h1>')
    
elif student_1_diff > student_2_diff:
    jupyprint(f'<h2>{student_2_name} wins $20!</h2>')
    student_2_money = student_2_money + 20
    jupyprint(f'<h2>{student_1_name} loses $20!</h2>')
    student_1_money = student_1_money - 20
    
elif student_1_diff < student_2_diff:
    jupyprint(f'<h2>{student_1_name} wins $20!</h2>')
    student_1_money = student_1_money + 20
    jupyprint(f'<h2>{student_2_name} loses $20!</h2>')
    student_2_money = student_2_money - 20
    
jupyprint("_________________________________________________________")
display(HTML(f'<b>{student_1_name} has ${student_1_money} left.</b>'))
display(HTML(f'<b>{student_2_name} has ${student_2_money} left.</b>'))

if (student_1_money <= 0) or (student_2_money <= 0):
    jupyprint("# GAME OVER!")
```
